Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray shows cardiomegaly (enlarged cardiac silhouette) and a pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm. In the context of pulmonary arterial hypertension, long-standing elevated pressure causes right ventricular hypertrophy and dilation (leading to cardiomegaly) and weakens the vessel wall, predisposing it to aneurysm or pseudoaneurysm formation. Thus, both findings are consequences of the underlying PA hypertension.
